content.text: Route-service's database spans are fast and only their volume is unusual, so that is probably a side effect rather than the fault. The seat-to-config client gap (about 420 ms against a 4 ms server span) looks more important. I'll open one slow travel-plan trace in full to see where the time goes.

input.query: WITH t AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-travel-plan-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' AND duration>3000000000 LIMIT 1) SELECT s.service_name, s.attr_span_kind kind, LEFT(s.span_name,60) sp, s.parent_span_id = '' AS is_root, s.span_id, s.parent_span_id, s.duration/1e6 ms, s.time FROM abnormal_traces s JOIN t USING(trace_id) ORDER BY s.time

content.text: The slow travel-plan trace spends about 3.8 s inside travel-plan's own code with no slow child, and seat-service's first slowdown (onset about 68 s) precedes travel-plan's (about 120 s). I'll check how seat's client calls to config evolve over time.

input.query: SELECT FLOOR(EXTRACT(epoch FROM time - (SELECT MIN(time) FROM abnormal_traces))/30)*30 AS sec, s.service_name, s.attr_span_kind kind, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(quantile_cont(s.duration,0.5)/1e6,2) p50, ROUND(quantile_cont(s.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95 FROM abnormal_traces s WHERE s.service_name IN ('ts-seat-service','ts-config-service') AND s.attr_span_kind IN ('Client','Server') AND s.span_name IN ('GET','GET /api/v1/configservice/configs/{configName}','POST /api/v1/seatservice/seats/left_tickets') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Seat's client calls to config are normally about 3.8 ms, but a subset spikes to 200–700 ms while config's own server spans stay near 3.5 ms. That points to delay on the seat→config path, not to config itself. Next I'll check whether travel-plan's slowness tracks its own time or its children's, over time.

input.query: WITH sv AS (SELECT trace_id, span_id, duration, time FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-travel-plan-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server'), ch AS (SELECT parent_span_id pid, SUM(duration) cd, COUNT(*) cn FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1) SELECT FLOOR(EXTRACT(epoch FROM sv.time - (SELECT MIN(time) FROM abnormal_traces))/60)*60 AS sec, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(quantile_cont(sv.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50_server, ROUND(quantile_cont(sv.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95_server, ROUND(quantile_cont(COALESCE(ch.cd,0),0.5)/1e6,1) p50_child_client_sum FROM sv LEFT JOIN ch ON ch.pid = sv.span_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: Travel-plan's median stays near 40 ms, but from about 120 s a subset of requests stalls for roughly 2.7–4 s. I'll check whether those stalls sit in travel-plan's own method time or in a specific child call.

input.query: WITH it AS (SELECT span_id, trace_id, span_name, duration, time FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-travel-plan-service' AND attr_span_kind='Internal'), chd AS (SELECT parent_span_id pid, COUNT(*) cn, SUM(duration) cd, MAX(service_name) csvc, MAX(span_name) cname FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1) SELECT it.span_name, CASE WHEN it.duration>1000000000 THEN 'slow' ELSE 'fast' END bucket, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(quantile_cont(it.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50_ms, ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(chd.cd,0))/1e6,1) avg_child_ms, ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(chd.cn,0)),2) avg_children, MAX(chd.csvc) csvc FROM it LEFT JOIN chd ON chd.pid = it.span_id GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Slow travel-plan requests carry about 3.7 s of time inside travel-plan's own method spans that no child span explains, so that looks like an in-process slowdown there. Before deciding, I'll check whether the route-not-found errors are new, comparing error logs in normal and abnormal periods.

content.text: Route-not-found errors already occur in the baseline (374 in normal), so they are background noise. I'll check travel-plan's JVM and GC metrics to see whether its 4 s stalls come from a runtime pause or from the method itself.

input.query: SELECT 'n' src, metric, COUNT(*) c FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-travel-plan-service' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'a', metric, COUNT(*) FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-travel-plan-service' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1 LIMIT 80

content.text: Travel-plan has no JVM metrics and its resource metrics are flat, so its 4 s stalls are in-process with no resource signal. Last, I'll confirm which user-facing endpoints from ui-dashboard are affected.
